scopedClaim: The 28 supplied six-component geometry vectors form exactly two numerical equivalence classes of 14 candidates each. Components 1 through 4 are identical across every candidate: [1, 1, 1, 0]. The classes differ only in components 5 and 6, with values (0, 0) or (0.2, -0.35). This is descriptor equivalence within this packet, not proof of complete geometric or physical equivalence.

preserved.archiveStatus: The supplied local descriptor registry lists all 28 candidates, no anomalies, and numerically valid toy responses; it explicitly does not establish global novelty.

informationLost: The packet provides no component names, units, coordinate convention, generating geometry, or descriptor construction rule; the physical meaning of individual components cannot be established.
Candidates sharing a vector cannot be distinguished by this representation; omitted geometric differences cannot be ruled out.
Flux, routing, eigenvalues, transport, implementation mechanisms, and experimental feasibility are not observed and cannot be inferred from these vectors.
uncertainty: Equality is exact numerical equality in the supplied JSON; measurement precision, robustness, and sensitivity to geometry changes are not supplied.
The scope is a three-site coherent-scattering toy. No inference to Kagome systems, chemistry, mechanical stress, hysteresis, fabrication, or experimental validation is justified.
This independent first pass uses a separate packet from the same deterministic simulator and curated candidate pool, so it is not statistical or security independence.

proposedTest.question: After component definitions and frozen source geometries are supplied, does an independent recomputation using geometry/1.0 reproduce the two reported descriptor classes for X00, X01, X02, and X03?
proposedTest.control: Freeze the descriptor definition, ordering, coordinate convention, units, source inputs, and numerical precision before recomputation. Include an exact duplicate of the X00 source geometry as a repeatability control; treat X00/X01 and X02/X03 as the two asserted same-vector pairs.
proposedTest.failureCriterion: The claim fails for the tested subset if any independently recomputed component differs from its supplied value by more than a prespecified absolute tolerance of 1e-10, or either asserted same-vector pair splits by more than that tolerance. A failing duplicate control makes the test inconclusive until repeatability is repaired. A passing result validates only descriptor reproduction, not unobserved physical properties.
